tips_feedback.why: Bob, a Yakuza player, used this tip as cover for switching from Vanilla to Medic. Town players should expect this excuse, and a Day 2 Vanilla claim made this way should be checked later.

lessons.tip: Combine the Fortune Teller's visited/visitor counts with the Cartographer's group sizes and one map. Every claimed visit has to fit both. Once they do, the Katana holder must be someone whose claimed visit lands on the victim, or someone with no visit claim who is linked into the victim's group. Each night this narrows the holder to 2-4 names. Ask every visitor in the group to post their target before anyone argues.

Treat a mid-game role switch as a strong tell, especially one made right after a map or count puts the player in the holder group (for example 'I was Vanilla, actually I'm Medic'). Spend the next exact-role check (Oracle, Profiler) on the switcher's new claim. A wrong result plus the switch is enough to hang.

A Profiler result's decoys are informative. One decoy is the role of another living player, so a non-Good decoy such as Diviner or Ritualist means that role may be alive. Compare it with any claim whose results look the same as that Evil role's (a Surveyor claim vs a Diviner). That is how a fake Surveyor gets caught.

As a Vanilla you can personally confirm any check made on you. Say so plainly to back that investigator, but also point out that a result copied from an already-public claim doesn't clear the investigator. Use your census and other overlaps to cross off names out loud, so confirmed info roles can see the eliminations.

Pick a fake claim on Day 2 that already covers any visit you might need later. A no-visit claim like Vanilla gives you nowhere to go once a map puts you in the victim's group, and switching claims then is fatal. If you might hold the Katana, claim a protector or visiting role from the start.

lessons.tip: Look at every decoy in a profile, not just the true role. One decoy is the role of another living player, so if a profile lists a role nobody has claimed (for example Diviner while someone claims Surveyor), that role is held by a living player. Say so publicly right away. Also check whether the not-in-game decoy rules out a claimed role. That is how a confirmed Lookout result also exposed the Yakuza Diviner.

Combine the Fortune Teller's visited/visitor counts with the Cartographer's group sizes every night. When the visitor count equals the number of claimed visitors, the Katana holder must be hiding the attack behind one of those claimed visits, usually a visit that 'happened' to land on the victim. That narrows the holder to 2-4 players, and other results can then split them.

Guessing a suspect's claimed role is the cheapest lie test there is. A WRONG result on a recent or switched claim (for example Vanilla to Medic) is close to decisive. A RIGHT result on a claim that was already public proves little to everyone else, so spend guesses on claims that are contested or haven't been checked.

Don't pick a fake claim whose results look exactly like an Evil role's. Surveyor results are identical to the Diviner's, so once a Diviner showed up anywhere (a profile, an archive), the cover fell apart. Also, never claim Vanilla and then switch to a power role once you're in a suspect group. Pick your claim on Day 2 and keep it.

Profile players whose claims would sort out the most others, such as one player of a census pair or someone linked to the holder. A profile can confirm two claims at once: here Alice's Census Taker plus Judy's Archivist decoy, with Ritualist not in the game. Keep your last token for a contested claim late in the game.

summary:
The Village won on Day 4. It hanged all three Yakuza on consecutive days (Heidi, Frank, Bob) and lost only three players along the way: Mallory and Erin to the Katana, and Dave, whose death came the same night the last Yakuza clue was gathered. Each day the town solved the night's visits in public, then used a different piece of information to choose between the remaining suspects.

**Day 2 (Heidi):** Several results lined up:
- Carol, the Fortune Teller, counted 6 players visited and 6 visitors.
- Dave, the Cartographer, reported visit groups of 4, 3, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1.
- Every visitor posted their target, and Olivia said who had role-blocked her.

Together these narrowed the Katana holder to Erin or Heidi. Heidi had planned a no-visit cover (Insomniac) that the Fortune Teller count could expose. She claimed last, as a Sheriff who "checked Mallory", the player the Katana killed. Sheriff was also missing from Judy's public archive list, while Lookout (Erin's claim) was on it. That archive mismatch broke the tie, and Heidi was hanged 11–1.

**Day 3 (Frank):** Frank was the Diviner, claiming Surveyor. Three results trapped him:
- Alice's Night 1 census found 2 Good among Frank, Grace and Niaj.
- Grace's Oracle guess confirmed Niaj as Vanilla Villager.
- Alice's Night 2 census found 0 Evil among Erin, Grace and Judy, which ruled out Grace as Yakuza.

On top of that, Olivia's profile of Erin listed Diviner as a decoy, and a decoy of that kind is the role of another living player. Frank was hanged.

**Day 4 (Bob):** Dave mapped Erin's visit group on Night 2, which put Bob in the group that contained the holder. Bob then switched his claim from Vanilla Villager to Medic. Grace tested it by guessing "Bob = Medic" and got WRONG. Alice's Night 3 census (2 of 3 Good among Bob, Grace and Ivan) backed this up, and Bob was hanged.

**Where the Yakuza went wrong:**
- Their Night 1 kill had no visit cover.
- They killed Erin, the Lookout who had already spent her information, rather than Alice (Census Taker) or Carol (Fortune Teller). Those two kept producing the counts that convicted Frank and Bob.
- Bob's Wiretap read nothing, because the town sent no private messages all game.
- Bob switched his claim once cornered.

**What the Village did well:** Everyone posted results in full and in public, and each Guilty vote rested on a concrete mechanical fit.

lessons.tip: When a Fortune Teller, Cartographer or Lookout might be in play, the holder's Katana visit needs a cover visit to the same target. Give the Katana to a teammate whose role visits, and point that role's action at the victim, so the kill adds no extra visitor or group link. If the holder claims no night action, one Fortune Teller count plus each visitor posting their target exposes them on Day 2.
lessons.evidence: Heidi held the Katana under a planned Insomniac cover that involves no visit. Carol's 6/6 count and Dave's group sizes left one unexplained visitor. Heidi was pushed into claiming 'Sheriff checked Mallory' after everyone else had claimed, which narrowed the holder to Erin or Heidi, and she was hanged.

lessons.tip: Solve the visit graph in public on Day 2. Every visitor posts their target, the Fortune Teller posts both counts, the Cartographer posts group sizes, and anyone role-blocked says so. After that, only one or two people can be hiding the Katana visit behind a claimed action. Then spend a Cartographer map on the most likely next Katana victim, so the holder's group is named the next morning.
lessons.evidence: On Day 2, Olivia's graph matched 4/3/2/1/1/1/1 and 6/6 exactly, leaving Erin or Heidi. Dave mapped Erin on Night 2, and she was killed that night. The map named the group Alice, Bob, Carol, Ivan and Olivia, which contained Bob, the holder.

lessons.tip: Before you fake-claim, check every public result that lists roles (archive, profiles, Surveyor or Diviner hits). Pick a role that fits that evidence, or at least isn't made unlikely by it. Claim early and in turn: a claim made after the visit math is public reads as fitted to it.
lessons.evidence: Lookout appeared on Judy's archive list and Sheriff did not. Judy and Ivan both pointed out that this made Erin's Lookout claim far more likely than Heidi's Sheriff claim, and that broke the tie. Heidi claimed last, and Dave and Erin both used that against her.

lessons.tip: Chain census results with confirmations. Once a census narrows a group to 'one non-Good among three', clear the others with any confirmed result: an Oracle hit on a claimed Vanilla, or a later census on overlapping players. The last name left is the target. Also note that a Profiler's decoys include the role of another living player, so a decoy like Diviner tells you that role is alive.
lessons.evidence: The three results above isolated Frank. Olivia's profile listing Diviner as a decoy matched Frank's fake Surveyor results, since a Diviner gets the same kind of result.

lessons.tip: Never switch claims once cornered. A switched claim is easy to test: an Oracle simply guesses the new role, and a WRONG result is decisive. If you hid as Vanilla, keep that claim and explain your graph edge some other way, or let a teammate absorb it.
lessons.evidence: Bob claimed Vanilla on Day 2. On Day 3, after Dave's map put him in the holder group, he switched to Medic. Grace guessed 'Bob = Medic' on Night 3 and got WRONG, and Bob was hanged 7–1 the next day.

lessons.tip: Kill the roles that keep producing information before the ones that are already spent. Census Takers, Fortune Tellers and Cartographers produce new evidence every night. A Lookout who has already posted their watch is worth less, and many players will visit them, which can make the victim's group a trap for the holder.
lessons.evidence: Yakuza killed Erin on Night 2, even though Bob had said 'we'll take Alice out soon'. Alice survived to Day 4. Her three census results convicted both Frank and Bob, and Carol's counts confirmed each graph.

lessons.tip: Keep discussion fully public and avoid private messages. A Wiretap or Eavesdropper then learns nothing, and every claim stays on the record where it can be cross-checked.
lessons.evidence: Nobody sent a private message all game, so Bob's Wiretap role, which was the Yakuza's planned source of information, gave them nothing to act on.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't defend a doomed teammate. If your team's votes can't stop the hang, vote Guilty with the town, because hidden Innocent votes show in the totals.
tips_feedback.why: Bob and Frank voted Guilty on Heidi (11–1), and Bob voted Guilty on Frank. Neither was linked to Heidi through the totals, so each stayed hidden for another day. They were caught later by role results, not by their votes.

tips_feedback.tip: Fake-claim a Village role whose tokens and real visits match yours. Never claim or name a Yakuza-only role, and never switch claims once cornered.
tips_feedback.why: Frank followed it: his Surveyor claim matched his real Diviner visits and results, and it held until census triangulation caught him. Bob broke the 'never switch' part by changing from Vanilla to Medic, and Grace's Oracle test exposed him straight away.

tips_feedback.tip: Never flatly deny a visit that an FT count, map group or Lookout could expose. Agree a cover in night chat, and move the Katana off any holder a watcher has named.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza ignored the first half on Night 1: Heidi's planned no-visit Insomniac cover was exactly what the Fortune Teller count exposed, and she was hanged. They did move the Katana off Frank on Night 2. The game shows the tip was right.

tips_feedback.tip: After a failed Katana attack, kill or block the likely protector instead of retrying blindly. Prioritize running counts (Fortune Teller, Census Taker) and Party Animals with block logs.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza killed the Party Animal on Night 1 but never killed Alice (Census Taker) or Carol (Fortune Teller), even though Bob suggested going after Alice. Those two produced the evidence behind the hangs of Frank and Bob. The game shows the priority advice was right.

tips_feedback.tip: Post your role, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and counterclaim any copier at once with your full log. Results held back look retrofitted.
tips_feedback.why: Almost every villager posted full results immediately, which let the town solve the Night 1 graph on Day 2. Grace held back her result and drew suspicion for it. Her results only became credible once she posted one she couldn't have copied from public claims.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete mechanical fit: an unexplained Evil read on a Vanilla claim, a broken visit claim, or a group result where elimination leaves one name. A role-block fully explains a missing result, so that is never a contradiction.
tips_feedback.why: Every hang was justified by a specific fit: the visit graph plus the archive for Heidi, census elimination for Frank, and the Oracle WRONG plus census for Bob. The town hanged three Yakuza with no misses.

issues.description: Last wills can only be written before Night 1, at the start of each Day, or during Day turns, so a night-acting role that dies on Night 1 can't record that night's action in its will. Mallory (Party Animal) died N1 with the will 'N1: (target TBD)' and raised this in post-game feedback. The rules work as written, but this makes action-log wills useless on the first night.

Some players talked as if roles are revealed on death, e.g. Judy: 'If Heidi flips as Sheriff, Erin hangs tomorrow' and Ivan: 'If Heidi turns out to be the real Sheriff'. Under R12, roles and alignments aren't revealed on death. Niaj corrected this during the same Day.

Minor misstatements of what results showed: Grace said 'Dave's maps show I visited nobody on either night' (Dave never mapped Grace; this can only be worked out from the group sizes), and Heidi said the archive showed '6 of the 11 other roles' (there were 12 other players). Neither changed the outcome.
